hn.originalTitle: Ask HN: What hardware are you using to run local LLMs?
hn.sourceOriginalText:
Figured I'd ask here because I have no doubt some of you are running some pretty cool, cost effective solutions for local models. Don't doubt some have mini data centers in their closets either haha, but just looking to get a view into what fellow HN'ers are using for their day to day work.

Comment 1: I have a 3090 w/ 24G VRAM, it supports flash attention and bf16, but is a bit old. I dont run generative models on it as they would be slow and inaccurate, but I do run embedding models, OCR, and system one (decision) models on it.

Comment 2: I got pretty good results with my 3090 on Qwen 27b. Yeah, the rack is completely unusable when you launch the llm, but i wouldn't say its slow. Btw, fellow 3090 user, some time ago i saw this: https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock Can't try it personally because windows, but maybe it will help you.

Comment 3: OK, that gpu-unlock is something I've never seen before and...wow. I did some research and NVidia really did kneecap their RTX for market segmentation. Grrrrr

Comment 4: Wow, this seems to speed up inference by 68% or something for me. Holy shit.

hn.summaryZh: 這篇來自 Hacker News 工程師討論，重點和 LLM 有關。適合用來快速了解社群正在討論的實作方向、工具變化或使用心得。
hn.sourceTextZh: 我想我會在這裡問，因為我毫不懷疑你們中的一些人正在為本地模型運行一些非常酷的、具有成本效益的解決方案。不要懷疑有些人的衣櫃裡有迷你資料中心，哈哈，但只是想了解一下 HN 的同事在日常工作中使用什麼。評論 1：我有一個 3090 w/ 24G VRAM，它支援 Flash Attention 和 bf16，但有點舊。我不會在其上運行生成模型，因為它們會很慢且不準確，但我會在其上運行嵌入模型、OCR 和系統一（決策）模型。評論 2：我的 3090 在 Qwen 27b 上得到了相當不錯的結果。是的，當你啟動 llm 時，機架完全無法使用，但我不會說它很慢。順便說一句，3090 用戶，前段時間我看到了這個：https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock 由於 Windows 無法親自嘗試，但也許它會對你有所幫助。評論 3：好的，GPU 解鎖是我以前從未見過的東西......哇。我做了一些研究，NVidia 確實對 RTX 進行了市場區隔。 Grrrrr 評論 4：哇，這似乎將推理速度加快了 68%，對我來說還是這樣。天哪。

hn.sourceOriginalText:
Anthropic’s growth just flattened (really)

Anthropic’s growth just flattened (really)

Look at the monthly numbers...

Henry Blodget Oct 15, 2026 37 4 Share Source: Regenerator estimates and news reports. Anthropic shared high-level Q3 financials with investors yesterday, report the NYT’s Andrew Ross Sorkin , Lauren Hirsch , and Sri Muppidi .

Revenue for Q3 was reportedly $16.8 billion.

At first glance, this number seems astonishing. And, in one sense, it is. It’s another jaw-dropping sequential gain for what is likely the fastest-growing company in history.

But, break the trend down into implied monthly growth, and the picture looks different.

Specifically, it seems Anthropic barely grew from July to September.

Anthropic’s sequential revenue growth in Q3, moreover, was smaller in absolute dollars than its (gobsmacking) growth in Q2.

So, for several possible reasons, Anthropic’s growth has meaningfully slowed.

This is likely another reason why the stocks of “neocloud” providers like CoreWeave are collapsing. CoreWeave, et al , have borrowed tens of billions of dollars on the assumption that demand for AI compute will continue to grow at rates way beyond consensus expectations for years.

Now, not only are interest rates soaring — raising the carrying costs of this debt — the near-term revenue growth for AI services may be flattening.

Anthropic’s reported revenue growth this year has been unprecedented:

Q1: $4.8 billion Q2: $11.6 billion (+$6.8B and +141%, sequentially) Q3: $16.8 billion (+$5.2B and +45%, sequentially)

Again, these numbers are astonishing.

But so are AI valuations and expectations.

Note that Anthropic added more revenue in Q2 than it did in Q3.

Note, too, that what matters most for Anthropic’s IPO valuation — and, likely, for the future trajectory of the AI bubble — is not what has happened but what will happen .

The key question is, “What do these numbers suggest about how fast Anthropic will grow from here ?”

These figures suggest that the market should temper its expectations, at least temporarily.

If we break down the quarterly figures above into monthly estimates and add one more reported data point — that Anthropic had a $65 billion annualized revenue run-rate in July — we see that Anthropic’s growth has flattened even more than the quarterly figures suggest.

Below are back-of-the-envelope estimates for Anthropic’s monthly revenue in 2026. They are based on the reported quarterly revenue figures as well as the $65 billion annualized revenue in July (which equates to ~$5.4 billion of July revenue).

Even the quarterly numbers suggest that Anthropic’s average monthly growth slowed from ~$760 million in Q2 to (“only”) $580 million a month in Q3.

But the “$65 billion annualized revenue in July” data point suggests the slowdown is even sharper.

If Anthropic did $5.4 billion in revenue in July and $16.8 billion in Q3, it likely only grew modestly in August and September.

According to DealBook, at its meeting with investors yesterday, Anthropic did not share an annualized revenue number based on September’s revenue. This suggests — to this analyst, anyway — that Anthropic did not think the September annualized revenue figure would show impressive-enough growth versus July.

Indeed, when we extrapolate the monthly figures, it seems Anthropic saw a sharp change in its growth trajectory in August and September.

It means that the growth of the leading company in the sector appears to have slowed sharply in the past two months.

The slowdown might at least in part be the result of seasonality. August, at least, tends to be a slow month. But it’s early in a product cycle to see such sharp seasonality. And September’s growth should have sped back up.

It might also mean that Anthropic is simply not able to keep up with the growth of demand. If this is the reason for the slowdown, it’s a high-quality problem, and it won’t have a long-term impact on the overall AI spending growth trajectory (or bubble).

But it may also mean that the near-term growth rate of AI spending is moderating — either because demand growth is moderating or because companies are using cheaper models from China for some of their AI needs. (Usage data suggests the latter is in fact happening).

If a slowdown in spending growth is the explanation, we should expect the wild investor enthusiasm for all things AI — and the colossal infrastructure spending growth supporting it — to also begin to moderate.

The end of all bubbles comes when supply begins to catch up
hn.titleZh: Anthropic 的成長剛剛趨於平緩
hn.summaryZh: 這篇來自 Hacker News 工程師討論，重點和 AI Agent 有關。適合用來快速了解社群正在討論的實作方向、工具變化或使用心得。
hn.sourceTextZh:
Anthropic 的增長剛剛趨於平緩（真的） Anthropic 的增長剛剛趨於平緩（真的） 看看每月的數字... Henry Blodget 2026 年 10 月 15 日 37 4 分享來源：Regenerator 估計和新聞報道。根據《紐約時報》的 Andrew Ross Sorkin、Lauren Hirsch 和 Sri Muppidi 報道，Anthropic 昨天與投資者分享了第三季的高階財務數據。據報道，第三季營收為 168 億美元。乍一看，這個數字似乎很驚人。從某種意義上來說，確實如此。對於這家可能是歷史上成長最快的公司來說，這是另一個令人瞠目結舌的連續收益。但是，如果將這一趨勢分解為隱含的月度成長，情況就會有所不同。具體來說，從 7 月到 9 月，Anthropic 似乎幾乎沒有成長。此外，以絕對美元計算，Anthropic 第三季的環比營收成長低於第二季（令人瞠目結舌）的成長。因此，由於多種可能的原因，Anthropic 的成長明顯放緩。這可能是 CoreWeave 等「neocloud」供應商股價暴跌的另一個原因。 CoreWeave 等人已經借了數百億美元的資金，因為他們假設人工智慧運算的需求多年來將繼續以遠遠超出共識預期的速度成長。現在，不僅利率飆升——增加了債務的持有成本——人工智慧服務的近期收入成長可能會趨於平緩。

Anthropic 今年報告的營收成長是前所未有的： 第一季：48 億美元 第二季：116 億美元（連續增加 6.8B 和 +141%） 第三季：168 億美元（連續增加 $5.2B 和 +45%） 這些數字再次令人震驚。但人工智慧的估值和預期也是如此。請注意，Anthropic 在第二季的營收比第三季增加了更多。還要注意的是，對於 Anthropic 的 IPO 估值以及人工智慧泡沫的未來軌跡來說，最重要的不是已經發生的事情，而是將會發生的事情。關鍵問題是，「這些數字表明 Anthropic 的發展速度有多快？」這些數據表明市場應該調整預期，至少暫時如此。如果我們將上述季度數據分解為月度預估，並添加另一個報告數據點——Anthropic 7 月份的年化收入運行率為 650 億美元——我們會發現 Anthropic 的增長趨於平緩，甚至比季度數據顯示的還要嚴重。以下是對 Anthropic 2026 年月度收入的粗略估計。這些估計是基於報告的季度收入數據以及 7 月份 650 億美元的年化收入（相當於 7 月份收入約 54 億美元）。即使是季度數據也表明，Anthropic 的月均成長從第二季的約 7.6 億美元放緩至第三季的（「僅」）每月 5.8 億美元。

但「7 月年化收入 650 億美元」的數據點表明，放緩幅度甚至更大。如果 Anthropic 7 月的營收為 54 億美元，第三季的營收為 168 億美元，那麼它在 8 月和 9 月可能只會小幅成長。根據 DealBook 報道，在昨天與投資者的會議上，Anthropic 並沒有分享基於 9 月營收的年化營收數據。無論如何，這表明——對於這位分析師來說——Anthropic 認為 9 月的年化收入數據與 7 月相比不會顯示出足夠令人印象深刻的成長。事實上，當我們推斷月度數據時，Anthropic 在 8 月和 9 月的成長軌跡似乎發生了急劇變化。這意味著該行業龍頭企業的成長在過去兩個月似乎大幅放緩。經濟放緩至少部分可能是季節性的結果。至少八月往往是一個緩慢的月份。但在產品週期的早期才會出現如此明顯的季節性。 9 月的成長應該會加快。這也可能意味著 Anthropic 根本無法跟上需求的成長。如果這是放緩的原因，那麼這是一個高品質的問題，並且不會對整體人工智慧支出成長軌跡（或泡沫）產生長期影響。

但這也可能意味著人工智慧支出的近期成長率正在放緩——要么是因為需求成長放緩，要么是因為企業正在使用來自中國的更便宜的模型來滿足其部分人工智慧需求。 （使用數據表明後者實際上正在發生）。如果支出成長放緩是原因，那麼我們應該預期投資者對人工智慧所有事物的狂熱熱情以及支持人工智慧的巨大基礎設施支出成長也將開始放緩。當供應開始趕上時，所有泡沫就會結束

hn.originalTitle: Ask HN: What hardware are you using to run local LLMs?
hn.sourceOriginalText:
Figured I'd ask here because I have no doubt some of you are running some pretty cool, cost effective solutions for local models. Don't doubt some have mini data centers in their closets either haha, but just looking to get a view into what fellow HN'ers are using for their day to day work.

Comment 1: I have a 3090 w/ 24G VRAM, it supports flash attention and bf16, but is a bit old. I dont run generative models on it as they would be slow and inaccurate, but I do run embedding models, OCR, and system one (decision) models on it.

Comment 2: I got pretty good results with my 3090 on Qwen 27b. Yeah, the rack is completely unusable when you launch the llm, but i wouldn't say its slow. Btw, fellow 3090 user, some time ago i saw this: https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock Can't try it personally because windows, but maybe it will help you.

Comment 3: OK, that gpu-unlock is something I've never seen before and...wow. I did some research and NVidia really did kneecap their RTX for market segmentation. Grrrrr

Comment 4: Wow, this seems to speed up inference by 68% or something for me. Holy shit.
